article_title: Building and Sustaining Talent: Creating Conditions in High-Poverty Schools That Support Effective Teaching and Learning
citation: Sarah Almy and Melissa Tooley. (2012). Building and Sustaining Talent: Creating Conditions in High-Poverty Schools That Support Effective Teaching and Learning. The Education Trust. https://edtrust.org/
title: T3 Turnaround Teacher Teams shared-leadership model
description: T3, developed by Teach Plus with Boston Public Schools, recruits experienced teachers with records of raising achievement into low-performing schools and trains them to use student data and facilitate teams in formal teacher-leader roles. “The T3 model requires at least 25 percent of a school’s teaching staff to be T3 teachers, to create a critical mass of teacher leaders,” with a T3 coach in each school and weekly teacher-facilitated common planning time.
requirements: Principal buy-in: principals must clearly define where they hold authority and where teachers exercise leadership and autonomy
At least 25 percent of the school’s teaching staff must be T3 teachers
constraints: With only one year of data, the report states it is unclear whether the initiative will have an ongoing influence on student progress.
target_learners: Students in persistently low-performing, high-poverty urban schools
target_learning_goals: Improving instruction and student outcomes through shared leadership and data-driven collaborative planning
examples: BPS implemented T3 at Orchard Gardens, Blackstone, and Trotter; one T3 teacher reported a calmer, more cohesive school climate and students happier and readier to work.
key_sources: Sarah Almy and Melissa Tooley. (2012). Building and Sustaining Talent: Creating Conditions in High-Poverty Schools That Support Effective Teaching and Learning. The Education Trust. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED543216

article_title: Comparing Two Story-Writing Mnemonic Strategies: A Randomized Control Trial Study
citation: Michael Dunn. (2013). Comparing two story-writing mnemonic strategies: A randomized control trial study. International Journal of Special Education, 28(3). https://www.internationaljournalofspecialeducation.com/
title: Think-Talk-Text (T3) mnemonic strategy for verbal pre-writing planning
description: T3 is a mnemonic strategy developed by Traweek (1993) with Dr Ginger Berninger in which students verbalize their story ideas aloud before encoding them as written text, with no story-structure schema such as the WWW, W=2, H=2 questions, and with children illustrating their texts after writing. The article describes it as "what I think, I can tell to others (i.e., verbalize aloud), and then write as text" and evaluates it in the randomized control trial.
requirements: Opportunity for students to verbalize story ideas aloud before writing
An interventionist or teacher to model and provide feedback on the strategy
constraints: T3 does not provide the WWW, W=2, H=2 story-content cue questions, which the author links to its smaller story-content effect
target_learners: kindergarten students in the original Traweek development
examples: In exit interviews, a T3 student explained that if children do not think or talk about their ideas first, they would not know how to write a story
key_sources: Michael Dunn. (2013). Comparing two story-writing mnemonic strategies: A randomized control trial study. International Journal of Special Education, 28(3). https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1024423
